headline: Southborough approved its FY27 tax rate, faced an FY28 budget deficit threatening service cuts, and evaluated $40 million Neary School renovation options.
synopsis: In November, the Select Board approved maintaining a single property tax rate of $14.54 per thousand for FY27, which is expected to raise the average single-family tax bill by 5.01 percent. Municipal and school officials turned their focus to FY28, preparing dual budget models to navigate an estimated $1.4 million deficit that could necessitate a Proposition 2 1/2 operating override or deep personnel reductions. The Elementary School Building Committee received updated architectural estimates showing realistic Neary School modernization costs will range between $33 million and $40 million, surpassing earlier $15 million concepts. The Planning Board extended its review and decision deadline on the proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse on Coslin Drive into December. Additionally, the town secured a state grant of up to $632,000 to cover half the cost of major park improvements at Fayville Memorial Park.

top_items.title: Select Board Adopts FY27 Property Tax Rate
top_items.why: The Select Board voted 4-1 to keep a unified single tax rate of $14.54 per thousand, resulting in an estimated 5.01 percent tax bill increase for the average single-family homeowner.
top_items.body: The Principal Assessor and Board of Assessors presented valuation data showing Southborough's total town valuation reached $4.072 billion, with average single-family home values rising 3.7 percent to $1,027,800. The Select Board debated adopting a split tax rate before approving the single tax rate 4-1, and voted 5-0 against residential and small commercial exemptions.

top_items.title: FY28 Budget Deficit May Force Operating Override
top_items.why: Departments drafted level-service and level-funded budget plans as officials warned an unaddressed $1.4 million deficit would force staff cuts across police, fire, and schools.
top_items.body: Town administration directed departments to submit two FY28 budget scenarios. Budget A maintains level services but leaves a $1.4 million shortfall requiring a Proposition 2 1/2 operating override. Budget B level-funds spending, which officials noted would force the elimination of an officer, cruiser, and dispatcher in the Police Department, reduce fire staffing enough to halt regular runs of the secondary ambulance, and eliminate approximately 15 school positions.

top_items.title: Neary School Renovation Estimates Reach $40 Million
top_items.why: Architectural estimates revealed that basic code upgrades at Neary Elementary will cost $32.9 million, while a comprehensive addition and renovation plan totals roughly $39.8 million.
top_items.body: Tappe Architects presented detailed cost analyses demonstrating that a previously contemplated $15 million budget cap for Neary School renovations is unworkable. Basic mechanical, electrical, and code upgrades require nearly $33 million, while the preferred addition and renovation option—which creates a full-size gym in the interior courtyard and expands learning spaces—is estimated at $39.8 million. Officials also discussed whether to seek MSBA funding in 2027 or pursue town-only financing.

top_items.title: Costco Public Hearings Extended into December
top_items.why: The Planning Board continued active hearings on traffic, stormwater, and lighting for the proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco, extending its decision deadline to December 18, 2026.
top_items.body: The applicant presented revised traffic analyses and site details for the proposed warehouse and 30-vehicle fueling facility at 21 Coslin Drive, prompting board and resident concerns regarding Route 9 intersection delays and truck cut-through traffic. Discussions also covered 36.6-foot light poles, site landscaping, and requested stormwater infiltration waivers. The board voted to continue the hearing to December 14 and extend its statutory decision deadline to December 18.

top_items.title: Fayville Memorial Park Awarded $632,000 State Grant
top_items.why: Southborough won a state grant covering half of the projected costs for a splash pad, dog park, and trail upgrades at Fayville Memorial Park.
top_items.body: The town was awarded up to $632,000 from the state Land and Water Conservation Fund for the Fayville Memorial Park improvement project. The Recreation Commission will seek matching Community Preservation Act funds at the 2027 Annual Town Meeting to fund the remainder of the project. Outstanding logistics include finalizing an off-street parking design along Central Street and addressing Article 97 legal requirements.

top_items.title: Zoning Proposal Advanced to Lift Senior Housing Cap
top_items.why: The Select Board voted to sponsor a Town Meeting warrant article that eliminates the town's 7 percent cap on 55-plus housing while requiring 12.5 percent affordability.
top_items.body: Drafted by the Affordable Housing Trust, the proposed zoning amendment removes the municipal cap on age-restricted developments, permits up to eight units per acre on parcels of at least two acres, and requires a 12.5 percent affordability mandate. The Select Board referred the article to the Planning Board and voted to sponsor it on the warrant. The Zoning Board of Appeals also reviewed the measure, deferring any endorsement until Planning Board hearings conclude.

top_items.title: Residents Oppose Senior Center Merger in Governance Study
top_items.why: A municipal governance listening session drew vocal opposition from residents against consolidating the Council on Aging and Senior Center into other municipal departments.
top_items.body: During a public listening session led by the town's governance consultant, participants debated municipal reporting structures and budget accountability. A large contingent of seniors and advocates strongly rejected proposals that would merge the Senior Center or Council on Aging with recreation or youth services, emphasizing that seniors comprise roughly 20 percent of Southborough's population with distinct service needs. The consultant will present final governance recommendations to the Select Board on December 15.
